description: Priya, a neighborhood costume maker, must decide whether to accept a local theater troupe's barter proposal for altering its costumes and finalize the work, compensation, equipment, deadline, and trust terms after a customary check-in with the people involved.

shared_context.S1: The neighborhood theater troupe needs costume work completed for its Sunday evening performance.
shared_context.S2: Priya has the tools and experience to do the costume work, and she decides whether to accept the arrangement and what terms to record.
shared_context.S3: Owen has approached Priya about arranging the work informally rather than signing a commercial contract.
shared_context.S4: Before making the final call, Priya follows her usual practice of asking each person present for any relevant details about the work, resources, and proposed terms.

PF1.text: Owen's exact proposal is for Priya to alter 14 costumes by hemming them and reinforcing their shoulder seams, in exchange for four rehearsal-space passes, with the finished costumes delivered by Sunday at 18:00.

PF2.text: Talia can reserve the community sewing room's industrial serger for Priya on Tuesday from 09:00 to 13:00, and using that machine is the practical way to finish all 14 reinforced hems on time.

PF3.text: Ravi previously worked with Owen on a show and confirms that Owen honored a promised barter of four rehearsal-space passes, so Priya can complete a reference check before accepting the same kind of exchange.

PF4.text: Mei would pay Priya exactly $420 in cash for the same 14-costume hemming and shoulder-reinforcement job, with delivery also due Sunday at 18:00.

acceptance_conditions: The arrangement must be accepted with Owen as the partner.
The work must cover exactly 14 costumes.
The service scope must be hemming and shoulder-seam reinforcement.
Compensation must be exactly four rehearsal-space passes.
Delivery must be promised for Sunday at 18:00.
The industrial serger must be reserved for the work.
A reference check concerning Owen's prior barter performance must be completed.
The $420 cash alternative must be recorded for comparison.
The serger reservation and reference check must be logged as commitments.
The accepted barter must cite Ravi's reference as justification.

content_checks.C2: decisions['costume_count'] == 14 and decisions['service_scope'] == 'hemming and shoulder-seam reinforcement'
content_checks.C5: decisions['industrial_serger_reserved'] == True and any(c['type'] == 'equipment_reservation' and c['target'] == 'Priya' for c in commitments)
content_checks.C6: decisions['reference_check_completed'] == True and any(c['type'] == 'reference_check' and c['target'] == 'Owen' for c in commitments)

provenance_checks.P1: 'PF3' in justification_fact_ids and 'PF3' in revealed and 'PF3' in credited_facts

decisive_facts.why: Owen's exact proposal changes the settlement to Owen, exactly 14 costumes, the specified hemming and shoulder-reinforcement scope, four rehearsal-space passes, and a Sunday 18:00 delivery.
The Tuesday 09:00-13:00 industrial-serger reservation changes equipment from unspecified to a required reserved machine for completing all 14 reinforced hems on time.
Ravi's prior-experience confirmation changes the trust step from unsupported to a completed reference check for Owen's four-pass barter, and supplies the fact Priya must cite.
Mei's offer changes the comparison record from no benchmark to exactly $420 cash for the same 14-costume job and deadline.
